extraction.body: Every week, the company has been introducing new devices and products. So here's a nifty roundup. Rather than hold a standard fall hardware event, Amazon has been announcing new products piecemeal over the last several weeks. It's a savvy move on the company's part to help keep its devices in consumers' minds instead of revealing a ton of stuff all at once that people may quickly forget about. Remember that microwave it once made? It seems the company's chief of Alexa and devices Panos Panay might agree. He recently told Engadget that "last year was a fine moment, but it turns out only two products really got any attention and everything else was just there." He also felt that the teams behind the overlooked products didn't get to take the pride that they, he felt, deserved. Well, we're here to help you keep up with all the things the company has announced in recent weeks. For a start, Amazon unveiled a new lineup of tablets that actually won't force you to resort to a workaround to access the Google Play Store . The latest batch of Kindles is here too, along with fresh Ring smart home gear and an updated Fire TV Stick 4K. Bee, a maker of AI note-taking devices, showed off its first new products since joining Amazon last year. Amazon has also teased that there are more Alexa-branded devices on the way . Here's a breakdown of the new devices Amazon announced so far in October. Amazon is transitioning away from Fire tablets to a new, more premium lineup of devices. Alexa tablets are now available in the US, Mexico, Canada, UK, Germany, France, Italy and Spain. They come in three sizes, the two smallest of which are primarily for entertainment purposes. The Alexa Tablet 8 (which starts at $230) has a 8.7-inch display, an 8-core CPU, 2-core GPU, 4GB of RAM and 64GB or 128GB of storage. It's 0.3 inches thick and weighs 16.4 ounces, so it's the most portable of the bunch. Amazon says it offers up to 14 hours of video playback and 19 hours of Kindle reading (more on that shortly) on a charge. Next up, we have the Alexa Tablet 11, which boasts a 2.5K, 11-inch display with a 90Hz refresh rate and a 16:10 cinematic aspect ratio. Along with an 8-core CPU and 2-core CPU, it has a fifth-gen MDLA NPU to support on-device AI processing. The tablet also has 8GB of RAM, the same storage options as its smaller sibling and dual Dolby Atmos speakers. The battery will deliver up to 15 hours of video playback, Amazon claims. This tablet starts at $330. Then there's the flagship model, the Alexa Tablet 12 Pro, which costs $500. Amazon says it's the most powerful model yet, with "three times faster processing and nine times faster graphics" than any of its previous tablets. The 12-inch, 280 PPI display has a 120Hz refresh rate and a 3:2 aspect ratio. The tablet has an 8-core CPU, 7-core GPU, 8th-gen MDLA NPU, 8GB of RAM and 128GB of storage. Battery life tops out at 16 hours for video playback and 20 hours for Kindle usage, Amazon says. As with the Alexa Tablet 11, the Alexa Tablet 12 Pro has a fingerprint sensor. There's an anti-glare option that's said to preserve detail and color accuracy. It's called Nanomatte and if you want that on your tablet, that'll run you $50 extra. The Alexa Tablet 12 Pro is designed more for productivity. To that end, there are accessories such as the $90 Alexa Tablet Pro Pen and the $150 Alexa Tablet Pro Keyboard, which connects to the device magnetically. All of the tablets have Alexa+ baked in, of course. You can opt in to a feature that allows you to ask the assistant about whatever is displayed on your screen. Amazon designed the Kindle experience (the Kindle app is installed by default) to be distraction free with reduced blue light. The Nanomatte display is said to give ebooks a paper-like feel, and you can add notes to books using the Pro Pen. There are also Kids versions of the Alexa Tablet 8 and Alexa Tablet 11. Like the other Alexa tablets, these have an aluminum design but come with a "kid-proof case" to help protect them. These versions also come with one year of Amazon Kids+ access. As expected, Amazon has bid adieu to Fire OS . Alexa tablets run on Android 16 with a custom layer on top. As such, they offer direct access to the Google Play Store. As someone who had to jump through hoops to access apps outside of the limited selection that Amazon itself offered on Fire tablets, that's a very welcome change. Unfortunately, though, it appears that Alexa tablets do not have a microSD card slot you can use to expand the storage. Amazon has new dedicated reading devices as well . The latest standard Kindle starts at $150 and it costs an extra $20 to remove the lockscreen ads. The six-inch model is a millimeter thinner than the previous model at 6.8mm and it weighs five ounces. The screen is flush with the casing, which is available in a fetching purple called Ube as well as Graphite. Amazon says the new entry-level Kindle is 30 percent faster at opening books than the previous model and that it can run for six weeks on a charge. A variant with an aluminum casing and double the storage (32GB) will run you $190. This comes in Alpine Sky and Seaglass Green color options. The latest Kindle Paperwhite has a seven-inch display, 16GB of storage, an adjustable warm light and what Amazon says is the highest contrast ratio on any Paperwhite to date. It's thinner and lighter than the previous model too. It costs $200, or $220 if you don't want lockscreen ads. Then there's the latest Paperwhite Signature Edition, which costs $250 and has no lockscreen ads, an aluminum back, 32GB of storage, auto-adjusting light and the option to double tap to turn pages. While the standard Paperwhite is only available in Graphite (also an option here), you can snag a Signature Edition in Seaglass Green. As for the updated Kindle Colorsoft, that has improved clarity and edge-to-edge color on the seven-inch display, Amazon says. Again, it's thinner and lighter than the previous model and there are no ads. The standard model with 16GB of storage is $290. The Colorsoft Signature Edition has an aluminum design, a Fig color option, 32GB of storage, an auto-adjusting front light and a double-tap-to-turn-pages feature. That'll run you $320. Both Colorsoft variants run for up to eight weeks on a charge, according to Amazon. Kids versions of the ereaders are available too. They have kid-friendly covers and a year of access to Kids+. In addition, Ring has updated several of its cameras. The Outdoor Cam 4K Plus, Spotlight Cam 4K Plus, Floodlight Cam 4K Plus and Indoor Cam 4K support Retinal 4K video capture . A new Pan-Tilt Indoor Cam 2K can rotate 360 degrees and tilt 175 degrees to automatically follow anything it detects to be moving. OK, Amazon announced this one in September , but isn't September 30 basically October? The company claims the new Fire TV Stick 4K is zippier than previous models. It says the device "turns on faster, apps launch over 35 percent faster, and content starts playing nearly 20 percent faster" than its predecessor and suggests it's faster than an unnamed rival dongle as well as some 4K smart TVs at playing content. This $60 Fire TV Stick 4K (Amazon wisely ditched the Select and Plus variants for this gen) is slimmer than earlier models and it can run on power from your TV's USB port. It has a 4-core processor, 8GB of storage, Alexa+ support and Wi-Fi 6. The company also redesigned the Fire TV remote. Bee announced its first two AI note-taking devices since Amazon bought the startup last year. The $75 Bee Frontier (which replaced the company's Pioneer model) is a Fitbit-esque wearable that has an estimated seven-day battery life and a IP67 rating for dust and water resistance. You can press a button to record audio of a conversation, and you can receive transcripts and summaries. If you hold the button, you can ask the AI assistant a question or create a voice note for yourself. Amazon says that, on Bee devices, "audio is never stored, cannot be accessed or shared, and users are prompted to gain permission from call participants each time a recording is started." As for the Bee Eclipse, that's a rectangular device that attaches to your phone magnetically. It has three microphones and a battery that's said to run for up to 21 days on a charge. Otherwise, it has much the same functionality as the Frontier. The Eclipse will run you $100 but, unlike the Frontier (which you can buy now), you'll have to wait for it. That device is "coming soon."

After years of teasers and warm-ups, Amazon finally pulled back the curtain on its new hardware lineup in New York. For a company that’s leaned so heavily on Alexa and its software smarts, the truth is that software only shines when the hardware around it does. Google has Nest. Apple has HomePods and Apple TVs. And Amazon? It’s long been the player trying to prove Alexa deserves a spot at the center of your living room. This year’s showcase felt different, more like Amazon finally putting its full hand on the table. The announcements went beyond shinier designs and brighter screens (though there was plenty of that). At the heart of it all was Alexa Plus , a new AI-powered assistant meant to tie the ecosystem together. From smarter speakers to larger displays to TVs that adapt to your space, here’s everything Amazon rolled out. Powered by Amazon’s AZ3 Pro chip, the new Echo Studio is tuned for sharper conversation detection and advanced AI models. It’s 40% smaller than the original but packs three full-range drivers, a custom woofer, and support for Dolby Atmos and spatial audio. For the first time, the light ring moves to the front. You can also connect up to five speakers with a Fire TV stick for what Amazon calls “Alexa Home Theater.” Price starts at $219.99, shipping October 29, with U.S. buyers getting early access to Alexa Plus–Amazon’s upgraded AI assistant. Alongside the Echo Studio comes the Echo Dot Max at $99.99, positioned directly against Apple’s HomePod Mini . The familiar sphere now has a flat face with controls and an LED ring. Inside, the AZ3 chip filters background noise, while a redesigned sound system delivers nearly three times the bass. It’s also the first Dot with two speakers: a high-excursion woofer and a tweeter. Preorders are open now, with availability starting October 29. Amazon didn’t skip its smart displays. The Echo Show 8 now carries a sharper LCD with wider viewing angles, while the Echo Show 11 feels like a natural step up from the old Show 10 with a 1080p screen. Both devices are slimmer, with thinner bezels, a 13MP camera, and front-facing speakers for clearer spatial audio. Unlike the motorized Show 10, these models stay put, though you can add a magnetic stand for tilt. The new Omni QLED Fire TVs are 60% brighter than the last generation, with Dolby Vision, HDR10 Plus, and adaptive color that shifts with your room lighting. They range from 50 to 75 inches, and pricing starts at $479.99. Amazon also refreshed its 2- and 4-Series Fire TVs , thinner and faster with a new quad-core chip, starting at $159.99. All now come with Alexa Plus built in for smarter searches and recommendations. Amazon is giving its Kindle line a makeover with three new Kindle Scribes, including the standout Kindle Scribe Colorsoft. Starting at $629.99, it offers up to two weeks of battery life and lets you highlight, draw, and write in colour when it arrives later this year. If that’s out of budget, there’s also a $429.99 entry-level Scribe and a $499.99 mid-tier model with a frontlit display. All three come with an 11-inch screen, slimmer bezels, a lighter design, and new AI tools that can even summarise your notes. Streaming is getting a bump too. The Fire TV Stick 4K Select is the first device powered by Amazon’s long-rumoured Vega OS, promising smoother performance, 4K playback, and HDR10 Plus support. Alongside the usual streaming apps, Amazon says Xbox Gaming, Luna, and Alexa Plus integration are on the way. Price tag? $39.99, and it’s already up for preorder. Ring’s latest lineup is all about sharper video. The company introduced a series of new cameras and doorbells with 4K resolution and its “Retinal Vision” technology. That includes the $249.99 Ring Wired Doorbell Pro 4K, $199.99 Outdoor Cam Pro 4K, $249.99 Spotlight Cam Pro 4K, and the $279.99 Floodlight Cam Pro 4K. For those who don’t need 4K, there’s a $179.99 Ring Wired Doorbell and a $59.99 Indoor Cam Plus with 2K video. New features also include AI facial recognition, Alexa Plus-powered greetings, and a quirky “Search Party” tool for helping neighbours locate lost dogs. Blink is shaking things up with the Arc, a $99.99 device that uses two lenses to stitch together a 180-degree panoramic view of your yard. No more switching between feeds, it’s all in one frame. The company also launched the Blink Outdoor 2K Plus and Blink Mini 2K Plus, both offering sharper resolution, better audio, colour night vision, and two-way talking with noise cancellation. Amazon’s 2025 fall showcase wasn’t just about rolling out shinier gadgets; it was about showing how Alexa Plus now runs through everything, from the speakers on your shelf to the TV in your living room, the Kindle in your bag, and the cameras on your front door. By blending hardware upgrades with AI smarts, Amazon is betting big on keeping its devices at the centre of your home life. Whether you’re after sharper sound, brighter screens, or just a splash of colour on your Kindle, this year’s lineup feels like Amazon laying down its vision for the next chapter of connected living. passages: With Alexa Tablets, revamped Kindles, upgraded Ring devices, refreshed Fire TV hardware and new AI-powered wearables already announced, Amazon’s fall product rollout is far from quiet.

The approach appears to align with the thinking of Panos Panay, Amazon’s head of Alexa and Devices, who recently suggested that large launch events often result in only a few products receiving meaningful attention while many others fade into the background.
Amazon also upgraded its streaming hardware lineup with a new Fire TV Stick 4K .
Amazon has also introduced children’s editions of the Alexa Tablet 8 and Alexa Tablet 11.

The broader theme running through every product launch is clear: Amazon is betting heavily on artificial intelligence, premium hardware experiences and deeper integration across its growing ecosystem of Alexa-powered devices.

The strategy has allowed each product to enjoy its own spotlight while keeping Amazon consistently in the tech conversation throughout October.

Amazon says audio recorded through Bee devices is not permanently stored and users are prompted to obtain participant consent whenever recordings begin.

Interestingly, Amazon appears to have dropped microSD card support, meaning storage expansion may no longer be possible.

For many users, this addresses one of the biggest limitations that affected previous Fire tablets.

sources.title: Apple announces all-new MacBook Pro with PROLED XDR display, its first touchscreen Mac - 9to5Mac
passages: Apple has officially announced the all-new MacBook Pro with PROLED XDR display , its first touchscreen laptop.
While Apple has innovated with multi-touch on the iPhone and iPad, the Mac has been resistant to touch input for years.
Back in March, Apple upgraded the standard 14- and 16-inch MacBook Pro laptops to the current M5 Pro and M5 Max chips.
MacBook Pro features Touch for the first time, bringing pros a whole new way to interact with their content.
Crafted specifically for the Mac, every touch interaction feels incredibly responsive and refined.

Everyday tasks are simple and intuitive, allowing users to scroll through a webpage with a natural swipe; pinch to zoom in on a photo; drag and drop slides from one presentation to another; and double-tap a window to fill the screen, or flick to tile it into place.
And the touch sensor is built directly into the display panel — not layered on top of it — reducing latency so users feel like they’re touching the content itself.
Apple also touts the use of a new hinge technology in the MacBook Pro, in part to support touch input without compromising on stability:
The existing MacBook Pro configurations from March stick around at the same prices.
You just lose OLED, the glowing Apple logo, and the thinner and lighter design.
The new machines still use Touch ID with no Face ID support.
We’ll have to keep waiting for Face ID and built-in cellular connectivity.
Pre-orders are available starting today with deliveries starting November 6.
The new machine was first hinted at by Apple on October 19 with the company’s “Pro and tell” experience teaser .
Earlier today, new Apple CEO John Ternus shared a “spotlight” teaser for the laptop as well.

The new machine was first hinted at by Apple on October 19 with the company’s “Pro and tell” experience teaser . Earlier today, new Apple CEO John Ternus shared a “spotlight” teaser for the laptop as well.
Read on for all the details about the new high-end laptop…
The new machine features a light-up Apple logo, tandem OLED, and touch input on the display.
It runs on the M5 Pro and M5 Max chips, like the existing MacBook Pro models without OLED touch displays.
John Ternus, who is rocking a new profile picture with the new Mac, shared the first look at the new machine on X:
We’re glowing with excitement over the new MacBook Pro. You’ve gotta touch it to believe it. pic.twitter.com/BLiGkGaefL
Apple previously used a glowing Apple logo on its notebook hardware for years until the 12-inch MacBook and 2016 MacBook Pro.
Pricing for the new laptop starts at $2899 for the 14-inch model. The 16-inch version starts at $3399.
Pre-orders are available starting today with deliveries starting November 6. You can find the product page for the new MacBook Pro here . The new machines are also available on Amazon .
Colors include silver or space black options with standard or nano-texture display configurations.

Beyond the new high-end laptop, Apple also announced the redesigned iPad mini , M6 iMac , and M6 14-inch MacBook Pro this week. Back in March, Apple upgraded the standard 14- and 16-inch MacBook Pro laptops to the current M5 Pro and M5 Max chips.
Apple calls the new design both thinner and lighter than the standard MacBook Pro models in the same size configuration.
The new MacBook Pros look awesome with glowing Apple logos. We’re so back. pic.twitter.com/Ce6G8EIVQF
The new MacBook Pro is the first to use what Apple calls a PROLED XDR display, replacing Mini-LED as the MacBook Pro display technology.

While Apple has innovated with multi-touch on the iPhone and iPad, the Mac has been resistant to touch input for years. The new MacBook Pro changes that with the first touchscreen Mac display. Here’s what Apple says about touch on the Mac.

MacBook Pro features Touch for the first time, bringing pros a whole new way to interact with their content. Crafted specifically for the Mac, every touch interaction feels incredibly responsive and refined. Everyday tasks are simple and intuitive, allowing users to scroll through a webpage with a natural swipe; pinch to zoom in on a photo; drag and drop slides from one presentation to another; and double-tap a window to fill the screen, or flick to tile it into place. And the touch sensor is built directly into the display panel — not layered on top of it — reducing latency so users feel like they’re touching the content itself.
Apple also touts the use of a new hinge technology in the MacBook Pro, in part to support touch input without compromising on stability:

Touch also introduces entirely new ways of working for pro users. Graphic designers can now use the entire display as their canvas, no longer constrained by the area of the trackpad when drawing; musicians can play software instruments right onscreen; and app developers can test how Touch performs in their iOS and iPadOS apps directly on the MacBook Pro display. And these new ways to interact with MacBook Pro work in tandem with the keyboard shortcuts and trackpad gestures pros know and love. In addition, a newly designed hinge provides greater stability while using Touch, and advanced video stabilization automatically smooths the camera feed in real time while using Touch on a video call.
In addition to touch as an additional input method, the new MacBook Pro also adopts the Dynamic Island in favor of the notch.
The Dynamic Island now comes to Mac, serving as the home for Spotlight, Live Activities, and Siri AI.

Not interested in touch? The existing MacBook Pro configurations from March stick around at the same prices. You just lose OLED, the glowing Apple logo, and the thinner and lighter design. Performance, however, is pretty much on par between versions as both offer M5 Pro and M5 Max chips.
The new laptops can be configured with up to 128GB of unified memory and 16TB of solid state drive storage.
Peak display brightness jumps from 1600 nits to 2000 nits for HDR content.

I honestly think this is a downgrade. Remember when Apple introduced the Touch Bar? It was supposed to be a big deal, but eventually Apple removed it. Now they’re adding a touchscreen to the MacBook. What’s the actual point?

If it supported the Apple Pencil, I could understand the appeal, especially for designers. But without it, I honestly don’t see much use for it. Maybe I’m wrong, but I’ve used touchscreen Windows laptops before, and I never really found it useful.

I can’t help wondering whether Steve Jobs would have approved of this direction. Apple needs a better marketing team that understands what people actually want, rather than adding a touchscreen that, in my opinion, offers very little practical use.

The 14-inch model is half a pound lighter at just 3 pounds even compared to 3.5 pounds for the same version of the previous design. The overall footprint is reduced as well with 0.59 x 12.24 x 8.52 inch dimensions compared to 0.61 x 12.31 x 8.71 inch dimensions when comparing 14-inch models.

The 16-inch model is notably lighter as well. The new design weighs in at 4 pounds even compared to 4.7 pounds for the previous design. Dimensions change to 0.63 x 14 x 9.62 inches compared to 0.66 x 14.01 x 9.77 inches between designs.
Playing piano on the touchscreen MacBook Pro pic.twitter.com/lDlwIeqErd

The new machines still use Touch ID with no Face ID support. Apple also doesn’t offer built-in cellular models of the new MacBook Pro. We’ll have to keep waiting for Face ID and built-in cellular connectivity.
You can find Apple’s press release for the new machines here . All configurations are available to order from Amazon .

sources.title: Apple announces touchscreen MacBook Pro with OLED display
passages: LOS ANGELES—Apple today announced and gave a first glimpse of its first major MacBook Pro redesign in more than five years.
As rumored, it includes an OLED display and, for the first time on macOS, a touchscreen—a change Apple has long debated. (Former CEO Steve Jobs famously was opposed.)

The OLED display (which Apple is, of course, calling the PROLED XDR) seems to be the real highlight here, compared to earlier models: It can achieve 2,000 nits in terms of maximum brightness, and Apple says it has a 10,000,000:1 contrast ratio.
References were made to burn-in protection, but details on which approach it’s taking for that weren’t yet shared.
The display retains the 120 Hz variable refresh rate of its predecessors.
Beyond that, the design is largely similar to the existing one, but there are a few notable differences.
Apple said when announcing it that the 14-inch model is just 3 pounds, down around half a pound from the previous model, depending on configuration.
Memory configurations top out where they did in previous MacBook Pro models with M5 Max: up to 128GB of RAM.
That said, storage can now go up to 16TB—if you can afford it.
Apple’s demonstration video showed users interacting with applications by reaching up to touch the screen, including file dragging and multi-touch gestures like pinch-to-zoom.

The M6 series has already arrived in other Macs, but it seems Apple is skipping them for this refresh; there were previously reports that Apple planned to hold off on updating the chip until the M7 series, which could have significant improvements for AI performance, just like the recently released A20 Pro chip for the iPhone does.
Second, the top-of-screen camera notch has been replaced by the small black cutout that Apple calls the Dynamic Island.
Presumably it works similarly to the one we’ve seen on the iPhone, expanding or contracting to show live activities and other information.
Finally, there’s a retro throwback: The Apple logo on the back of the lid glows like the logo on MacBooks of yore.

Apple’s demonstration video showed users interacting with applications by reaching up to touch the screen, including file dragging and multi-touch gestures like pinch-to-zoom. It does not appear to be a 2-in-1 convertible design, though; all the footage was of people reaching up to touch the screen in a normal laptop configuration.

Beyond that, the design is largely similar to the existing one, but there are a few notable differences. First, it’s much lighter. Apple said when announcing it that the 14-inch model is just 3 pounds, down around half a pound from the previous model, depending on configuration.

Second, the top-of-screen camera notch has been replaced by the small black cutout that Apple calls the Dynamic Island. Presumably it works similarly to the one we’ve seen on the iPhone, expanding or contracting to show live activities and other information.
Finally, there’s a retro throwback: The Apple logo on the back of the lid glows like the logo on MacBooks of yore.

In terms of specs, this refresh includes the M5 Pro and M5 Max chips—the same ones in the previous refresh. extraction.body: Apple has officially introduced the all-new MacBook Pro, marking a major milestone as the company's first touchscreen Mac. Powered by the M5 Pro and M5 Max chips, this high-end laptop features a completely redesigned, thinner, and lighter form factor alongside cutting-edge display technology. The headline feature is the PROLED XDR display, which replaces previous Mini-LED panels with tandem OLED technology. This upgrade increases peak HDR brightness to 2000 nits and introduces intuitive touch capabilities to the macOS ecosystem for the first time. The physical design also revives the classic light-up Apple logo on the exterior lid. The 14-inch model weighs 3 pounds with dimensions of 0.59 x 12.24 x 8.52 inches, while the 16-inch model weighs 4 pounds with dimensions of 0.63 x 14 x 9.62 inches. Biometric security continues to rely on Touch ID, as Face ID and built-in cellular connectivity are not included in this release. Available in silver and space black, finishes can be paired with standard or nano-texture display options. Pre-orders are open immediately, with official deliveries scheduled to begin on November 6.

extraction.body: Apple today announced a new high-end MacBook Pro , which is available in 14-inch and 16-inch sizes. The new device has a PROLED XDR display that supports touch gestures, and a glowing rear Apple logo. Pricing on the ‌MacBook Pro‌ starts at $2,899 for the 14-inch model and $3,399 for the 16-inch model. Apple says the ‌MacBook Pro‌ has the "world's best display in a pro laptop." The PROLED display uses tandem OLED paired with advanced algorithms in the display engine and factory calibration for "exceptional brightness, striking contrast, and vivid true-to-life colors." The display offers up to 2000 nits peak HDR and SDR brightness, along with a 10,000,000:1 contrast ratio. A display engine controls the color and luminance of each pixel, compensating for content, temperature, environment, and pixel use. ProMotion technology is available with refresh rates ranging from 10Hz to 120Hz. An antireflective coating cuts down on glare in bright lighting conditions, and there is an option to order the new ‌MacBook Pro‌ with a nano-texture display. A touch sensor is built directly in the display panel, so there is no added latency. Apple says touch interactions feel "incredibly responsive and refined." Users can scroll through a webpage with a swipe, pinch to zoom in on a photo, drag and drop slides from one presentation to another, and double-tap a window to have it fill the screen. A new hinge design offers more stability when using touch, and advanced video stabilization smooths the camera feed when using touch on a video call. Apple says macOS automatically translates touch into clicks, so many existing apps will work with touch right away. The ‌MacBook Pro‌ is up to 1mm slimmer than the existing version, and it is lighter weight at just three pounds for the 14-inch model and four pounds for the 16-inch model. There is no more notch, with Apple instead adding a small Dynamic Island that takes up less space. The ‌Dynamic Island‌ houses Spotlight, Live Activities, and Siri AI. Like on the iPhone, it offers a quick way to see and interact with important information. Smaller bezels mean the 16-inch ‌MacBook Pro‌ display is now 16.3 inches in size, while the 14-inch ‌MacBook Pro‌ is now 14.2 inches. The new ‌MacBook Pro‌ uses the same M5 Pro and M5 Max chips as the ‌MacBook Pro‌ models announced back in March, but there is a redesigned thermal architecture that directs warm air away from the display. There is support for up to 128GB of unified memory, and a new six-speaker sound system with 50 percent deeper bass. There are three Thunderbolt 5 ports, HDMI, an SDXC card slot, MagSafe , and a headphone jack. The new machines support up to four external displays and come with Wi-Fi 7 and Bluetooth 6. Fast charging allows the ‌MacBook Pro‌ to be charged to 50 percent in 30 minutes, and up to 16TB storage is available. Apple is selling the ‌OLED‌ ‌MacBook Pro‌ models alongside the existing mini-LED models and the new M6 14-inch ‌MacBook Pro‌. Pre-orders are available now, with a launch coming on Friday, November 6. coreStoryFacts.text: Apple has officially announced the all-new MacBook Pro with PROLED XDR display , its first touchscreen laptop.
While Apple has innovated with multi-touch on the iPhone and iPad, the Mac has been resistant to touch input for years.
Back in March, Apple upgraded the standard 14- and 16-inch MacBook Pro laptops to the current M5 Pro and M5 Max chips.
MacBook Pro features Touch for the first time, bringing pros a whole new way to interact with their content.
Crafted specifically for the Mac, every touch interaction feels incredibly responsive and refined.

Everyday tasks are simple and intuitive, allowing users to scroll through a webpage with a natural swipe; pinch to zoom in on a photo; drag and drop slides from one presentation to another; and double-tap a window to fill the screen, or flick to tile it into place.
And the touch sensor is built directly into the display panel — not layered on top of it — reducing latency so users feel like they’re touching the content itself.
Apple also touts the use of a new hinge technology in the MacBook Pro, in part to support touch input without compromising on stability:
The existing MacBook Pro configurations from March stick around at the same prices.
You just lose OLED, the glowing Apple logo, and the thinner and lighter design.
The new machines still use Touch ID with no Face ID support.
We’ll have to keep waiting for Face ID and built-in cellular connectivity.
Pre-orders are available starting today with deliveries starting November 6.
The new machine was first hinted at by Apple on October 19 with the company’s “Pro and tell” experience teaser .
Earlier today, new Apple CEO John Ternus shared a “spotlight” teaser for the laptop as well.
Remember when Apple introduced the Touch Bar?
It was supposed to be a big deal, but eventually Apple removed it.
Now they’re adding a touchscreen to the MacBook.
Apple’s Mac lineup consists of MacBook, MacBoo…
The new MacBook Pros look awesome with glowing Apple logos.
Touch also introduces entirely new ways of working for pro users.

In addition, a newly designed hinge provides greater stability while using Touch, and advanced video stabilization automatically smooths the camera feed in real time while using Touch on a video call.
Playing piano on the touchscreen MacBook Pro pic.twitter.com/lDlwIeqErd
I can’t help wondering whether Steve Jobs would have approved of this direction.

LOS ANGELES—Apple today announced and gave a first glimpse of its first major MacBook Pro redesign in more than five years.
As rumored, it includes an OLED display and, for the first time on macOS, a touchscreen—a change Apple has long debated. (Former CEO Steve Jobs famously was opposed.)

The OLED display (which Apple is, of course, calling the PROLED XDR) seems to be the real highlight here, compared to earlier models: It can achieve 2,000 nits in terms of maximum brightness, and Apple says it has a 10,000,000:1 contrast ratio.
References were made to burn-in protection, but details on which approach it’s taking for that weren’t yet shared.
The display retains the 120 Hz variable refresh rate of its predecessors.
Beyond that, the design is largely similar to the existing one, but there are a few notable differences.
Apple said when announcing it that the 14-inch model is just 3 pounds, down around half a pound from the previous model, depending on configuration.
Memory configurations top out where they did in previous MacBook Pro models with M5 Max: up to 128GB of RAM.
That said, storage can now go up to 16TB—if you can afford it.
Apple’s demonstration video showed users interacting with applications by reaching up to touch the screen, including file dragging and multi-touch gestures like pinch-to-zoom.

The M6 series has already arrived in other Macs, but it seems Apple is skipping them for this refresh; there were previously reports that Apple planned to hold off on updating the chip until the M7 series, which could have significant improvements for AI performance, just like the recently released A20 Pro chip for the iPhone does.
Second, the top-of-screen camera notch has been replaced by the small black cutout that Apple calls the Dynamic Island.
Presumably it works similarly to the one we’ve seen on the iPhone, expanding or contracting to show live activities and other information.
Finally, there’s a retro throwback: The Apple logo on the back of the lid glows like the logo on MacBooks of yore.

Read on for all the details about the new high-end laptop…
The new machine features a light-up Apple logo, tandem OLED, and touch input on the display.

Apple previously used a glowing Apple logo on its notebook hardware for years until the 12-inch MacBook and 2016 MacBook Pro.

The new MacBook Pro is the first to use what Apple calls a PROLED XDR display, replacing Mini-LED as the MacBook Pro display technology.

While Apple has innovated with multi-touch on the iPhone and iPad, the Mac has been resistant to touch input for years. The new MacBook Pro changes that with the first touchscreen Mac display. Here’s what Apple says about touch on the Mac.

MacBook Pro features Touch for the first time, bringing pros a whole new way to interact with their content. Crafted specifically for the Mac, every touch interaction feels incredibly responsive and refined. Everyday tasks are simple and intuitive, allowing users to scroll through a webpage with a natural swipe; pinch to zoom in on a photo; drag and drop slides from one presentation to another; and double-tap a window to fill the screen, or flick to tile it into place. And the touch sensor is built directly into the display panel — not layered on top of it — reducing latency so users feel like they’re touching the content itself.
Apple also touts the use of a new hinge technology in the MacBook Pro, in part to support touch input without compromising on stability:

Touch also introduces entirely new ways of working for pro users. Graphic designers can now use the entire display as their canvas, no longer constrained by the area of the trackpad when drawing; musicians can play software instruments right onscreen; and app developers can test how Touch performs in their iOS and iPadOS apps directly on the MacBook Pro display. And these new ways to interact with MacBook Pro work in tandem with the keyboard shortcuts and trackpad gestures pros know and love. In addition, a newly designed hinge provides greater stability while using Touch, and advanced video stabilization automatically smooths the camera feed in real time while using Touch on a video call.
In addition to touch as an additional input method, the new MacBook Pro also adopts the Dynamic Island in favor of the notch.
The Dynamic Island now comes to Mac, serving as the home for Spotlight, Live Activities, and Siri AI.

Not interested in touch? The existing MacBook Pro configurations from March stick around at the same prices. You just lose OLED, the glowing Apple logo, and the thinner and lighter design. Performance, however, is pretty much on par between versions as both offer M5 Pro and M5 Max chips.
The new laptops can be configured with up to 128GB of unified memory and 16TB of solid state drive storage.
Peak display brightness jumps from 1600 nits to 2000 nits for HDR content.

I honestly think this is a downgrade. Remember when Apple introduced the Touch Bar? It was supposed to be a big deal, but eventually Apple removed it. Now they’re adding a touchscreen to the MacBook. What’s the actual point?

If it supported the Apple Pencil, I could understand the appeal, especially for designers. But without it, I honestly don’t see much use for it. Maybe I’m wrong, but I’ve used touchscreen Windows laptops before, and I never really found it useful.

I can’t help wondering whether Steve Jobs would have approved of this direction. Apple needs a better marketing team that understands what people actually want, rather than adding a touchscreen that, in my opinion, offers very little practical use.

The 14-inch model is half a pound lighter at just 3 pounds even compared to 3.5 pounds for the same version of the previous design. The overall footprint is reduced as well with 0.59 x 12.24 x 8.52 inch dimensions compared to 0.61 x 12.31 x 8.71 inch dimensions when comparing 14-inch models.

The 16-inch model is notably lighter as well. The new design weighs in at 4 pounds even compared to 4.7 pounds for the previous design. Dimensions change to 0.63 x 14 x 9.62 inches compared to 0.66 x 14.01 x 9.77 inches between designs.
Playing piano on the touchscreen MacBook Pro pic.twitter.com/lDlwIeqErd

The new machines still use Touch ID with no Face ID support. Apple also doesn’t offer built-in cellular models of the new MacBook Pro. We’ll have to keep waiting for Face ID and built-in cellular connectivity.

The company is looking to build new commercial opportunities around conversational search while protecting the growth of its core advertising business. The expansion, announced alongside Alphabet’s third-quarter 2026 results, will bring ads in AI Mode to Australia, Canada, India, Kenya, Malaysia, New Zealand, Nigeria, Pakistan, the Philippines and Singapore. Google plans to extend the rollout to Brazil, Mexico and the United Kingdom in the fourth quarter. In the US, it is introducing multiturn ads that can appear in follow-up queries within AI Mode. The move comes as Google Search advertising growth moderates even as usage of its AI-powered features increases. Search and other advertising revenue rose 12% year on year to $63.35 billion in the September quarter, compared with 17% growth in the previous quarter. YouTube advertising revenue increased 9.2% to $11.21 billion, while total Google advertising revenue grew 10.6% to $82.01 billion. AI Mode allows users to explore questions through longer, more conversational interactions, creating a different environment for product discovery and commercial intent than a conventional search results page. From search results to conversational discovery Google said queries in AI Mode are, on average, three times longer than traditional Search queries. The company believes AI helps it understand what users are looking for and connect them with businesses and services that match their needs. Google said its research indicates that users find ads in AI Mode relevant and that click-through rates for sponsored and organic product-list items are already similar. The expansion signals Google's intention to bring advertising into more of the AI-assisted journey, rather than limit monetisation to conventional search results. Longer queries can give the system more context about what a user wants, potentially creating opportunities for advertisers to reach consumers as they compare products, evaluate options or narrow down a purchase. However, the company has not disclosed how much revenue AI Mode advertising currently generates or how much it expects the international rollout to contribute. Pichai says AI is driving Search usage to a five-year high The advertising push comes against a broader backdrop of AI-led growth across Alphabet. On the company's Q3 earnings call, Google and Alphabet CEO Sundar Pichai said Search was seeing strong momentum, with AI investments driving higher usage and growth in overall queries, including commercial queries. “Our AI investments are driving overall Search query growth, including commercial queries. In fact, our year-over-year query growth rate is the highest it’s been in the last five years,” Pichai said. He described the company's strategy as building a seamless experience across AI Overviews, AI Mode and traditional Search, as users increasingly adopt new ways of finding information. Their queries are longer, personalized, and multimodal,” he said. Pichai added that one in five AI Mode searches globally involves voice, images or documents, while Google now handles more than 50 billion visual searches a month. These shifts matter commercially because Google's advertising model has historically depended on matching search queries with relevant ads. As the interface evolves from a list of links towards AI-generated responses and more extended interactions, the company needs to determine how advertising fits into those experiences and how it can deliver value to businesses. Alphabet's growth increasingly spans advertising and AI infrastructure Alphabet reported third-quarter revenue of $127.58 billion, up 25% year on year. Google Services, which includes Search, YouTube, subscriptions and devices, generated $96.3 billion, an increase of 11%. Google Cloud revenue more than doubled to $30.71 billion, driven by demand for AI infrastructure and enterprise AI solutions. Pichai said the company was working to bring more capacity online to meet long-term demand. “We had a strong quarter and are now on a half-trillion dollar revenue run rate,” he said. “Our deep full stack approach is driving momentum across the business, with Alphabet revenues growing 25% year-over year.” The Gemini app has reached one billion users, according to Pichai, while Google's first-party model APIs are processing nearly 32 billion tokens per minute, more than four times the volume a year earlier. The company is investing heavily to support this growth. Alphabet's capital expenditure reached $51.4 billion in the quarter, primarily reflecting spending on data centres and AI infrastructure. It maintained its 2026 capital expenditure outlook of $195 billion to $205 billion and said spending would increase significantly in 2027. Net income available to common stockholders fell 25% to $26.17 billion. Alphabet attributed the decline in part to an $8.7 billion net loss on equity securities, highlighting that the profit movement was not solely a reflection of its operating performance. extraction.body: Google is expanding advertising in its AI-powered Search experience, AI Mode, to India and nine other markets. The company is looking to build new commercial opportunities around conversational search while protecting the growth of its core advertising business. The expansion, announced alongside Alphabet’s third-quarter 2026 results, will bring ads in AI Mode to Australia, Canada, India, Kenya, Malaysia, New Zealand, Nigeria, Pakistan, the Philippines and Singapore. Google plans to extend the rollout to Brazil, Mexico and the United Kingdom in the fourth quarter. In the US, it is introducing multiturn ads that can appear in follow-up queries within AI Mode. The move comes as Google Search advertising growth moderates even as usage of its AI-powered features increases. Search and other advertising revenue rose 12% year on year to $63.35 billion in the September quarter, compared with 17% growth in the previous quarter. YouTube advertising revenue increased 9.2% to $11.21 billion, while total Google advertising revenue grew 10.6% to $82.01 billion. AI Mode allows users to explore questions through longer, more conversational interactions, creating a different environment for product discovery and commercial intent than a conventional search results page. From search results to conversational discovery Google said queries in AI Mode are, on average, three times longer than traditional Search queries. The company believes AI helps it understand what users are looking for and connect them with businesses and services that match their needs. Google said its research indicates that users find ads in AI Mode relevant and that click-through rates for sponsored and organic product-list items are already similar. The expansion signals Google's intention to bring advertising into more of the AI-assisted journey, rather than limit monetisation to conventional search results. Longer queries can give the system more context about what a user wants, potentially creating opportunities for advertisers to reach consumers as they compare products, evaluate options or narrow down a purchase. However, the company has not disclosed how much revenue AI Mode advertising currently generates or how much it expects the international rollout to contribute. Pichai says AI is driving Search usage to a five-year high The advertising push comes against a broader backdrop of AI-led growth across Alphabet. On the company's Q3 earnings call, Google and Alphabet CEO Sundar Pichai said Search was seeing strong momentum, with AI investments driving higher usage and growth in overall queries, including commercial queries. “Our AI investments are driving overall Search query growth, including commercial queries. In fact, our year-over-year query growth rate is the highest it’s been in the last five years,” Pichai said. He described the company's strategy as building a seamless experience across AI Overviews, AI Mode and traditional Search, as users increasingly adopt new ways of finding information. Their queries are longer, personalized, and multimodal,” he said. Pichai added that one in five AI Mode searches globally involves voice, images or documents, while Google now handles more than 50 billion visual searches a month. These shifts matter commercially because Google's advertising model has historically depended on matching search queries with relevant ads. As the interface evolves from a list of links towards AI-generated responses and more extended interactions, the company needs to determine how advertising fits into those experiences and how it can deliver value to businesses. Alphabet's growth increasingly spans advertising and AI infrastructure Alphabet reported third-quarter revenue of $127.58 billion, up 25% year on year. Google Services, which includes Search, YouTube, subscriptions and devices, generated $96.3 billion, an increase of 11%. Google Cloud revenue more than doubled to $30.71 billion, driven by demand for AI infrastructure and enterprise AI solutions. Pichai said the company was working to bring more capacity online to meet long-term demand. “We had a strong quarter and are now on a half-trillion dollar revenue run rate,” he said. “Our deep full stack approach is driving momentum across the business, with Alphabet revenues growing 25% year-over year.” The Gemini app has reached one billion users, according to Pichai, while Google's first-party model APIs are processing nearly 32 billion tokens per minute, more than four times the volume a year earlier. The company is investing heavily to support this growth. Alphabet's capital expenditure reached $51.4 billion in the quarter, primarily reflecting spending on data centres and AI infrastructure. It maintained its 2026 capital expenditure outlook of $195 billion to $205 billion and said spending would increase significantly in 2027. Net income available to common stockholders fell 25% to $26.17 billion. Alphabet attributed the decline in part to an $8.7 billion net loss on equity securities, highlighting that the profit movement was not solely a reflection of its operating performance. The next test for Google's advertising model Google's AI Mode rollout is part of a wider effort to extend its commercial ecosystem into new forms of discovery and task completion.

passages: The 14-inch and 16-inch MacBook Pros are available for pre-order now and will ship on Nov.
The 14-incher will start at $2,899, while the 16-incher will start at $3,399.
The systems use Apple's existing M5 Pro and M5 Max chips, and go up to 16TB of storage and 128GB of memory.
These systems also feature the first redesigns for the MacBook Pro since 2021, when the M1 Pro and M1 Max launched in what has become a familiar design with a notch.
These new models include the Dynamic Island around the webcam, similar to the iPhone, which can be used for real-time notifications.

Apple finally has touchscreen laptops. At an event in Los Angeles, the company detailed its new MacBook Pros featuring OLED XDR displays that you can control with your fingers. The 14-inch and 16-inch MacBook Pros are available for pre-order now and will ship on Nov. 6. The 14-incher will start at $2,899, while the 16-incher will start at $3,399. The systems use Apple's existing M5 Pro and M5 Max chips, and go up to 16TB of storage and 128GB of memory. These systems also feature the first redesigns for the MacBook Pro since 2021, when the M1 Pro and M1 Max launched in what has become a familiar design with a notch. These new models include the Dynamic Island around the webcam, similar to the iPhone, which can be used for real-time notifications. They also have light-up Apple logos, which we haven't seen on a MacBook Pro since 2016. The PROLED XDR display comes in 14.2-and 16.3-inch sizes, with ProMotion allowing for refresh rates between 10 Hz and 120 Hz. Apple claims 2,000 nits of peak brightness and a 10,000,000:1 contrast ratio for intensely deep blacks. The 14-inch MacBook Pro is 3 pounds, about half a pound less than the existing version, while the 16-inch MacBook Pro is 4 pounds, or 0.7 pounds lighter than it was before. Apple's bezels are also less noticeable than before. The hinge seems to be a point of pride (that's the second time this month, after the iPhone Duo). In this case, it's that the screen is less prone to wobble when you touch it. The new laptops are only slightly thinner than their predecessor. Apple claims that the 16-inch model is "nearly a millimeter thinner" and the 14-incher is "half a millimeter thinner." Apple attributes those shavings to OLED's display stack. Apple's own apps are already set to work with touch out of the box, and the company says many other apps will already work right away, including Notion, Canva, Zoom, Microsoft Word, Excel, PowerPoint, Adobe Lightroom, DaVinci Resolve, Blender, and more. Get Tom's Hardware's best news and in-depth reviews, straight to your inbox. Apple already had the best speakers in a laptop, and now it's promising improvements: 50% deeper bass and new tweeters for clearer sound. There's even dedicated audio tuning for people who want to use the speakers with their laptop lid closed. The significant change to the Mac is another in a flurry of launches for new CEO John Ternus, who also recently introduced the iPhone 18 Pro; the foldable iPhone Duo; Apple Watch Series 12 and Ultra 4; HomeView; and a new iPad Mini, also with an OLED panel. The devices follow a long resistance to touchscreen laptops from Apple. Former CEO Steve Jobs, at an event introducing Mac OS X Lion in 2010, called laptops with touchscreens "ergonomically terrible" , claiming that "after an extended period of time, your arm wants to fall off." (HomeView, Apple's smart home manager, has a vertical touchscreen and no one has made a peep about that. The iPad, too, has been vertical on Apple's keyboards, though some of those include touchpads as well). The Mac resisted a touchscreen throughout former CEO Tim Cook's tenure, as well, though these new laptops definitely were developed under his leadership. In the last decade, touchscreens have become a common feature on laptops running Windows, and Microsoft's latest operating system, Windows 11 , was designed to be slightly more touch-friendly than its predecessors. Apple finally has touchscreen laptops. At an event in Los Angeles, the company detailed its new MacBook Pros featuring OLED XDR displays that you can control with your fingers.

The 14-inch and 16-inch MacBook Pros are available for pre-order now and will ship on Nov. 6. The 14-incher will start at $2,899, while the 16-incher will start at $3,399. The systems use Apple's existing M5 Pro and M5 Max chips, and go up to 16TB of storage and 128GB of memory.

These systems also feature the first redesigns for the MacBook Pro since 2021, when the M1 Pro and M1 Max launched in what has become a familiar design with a notch. These new models include the Dynamic Island around the webcam, similar to the iPhone, which can be used for real-time notifications. They also have light-up Apple logos, which we haven't seen on a MacBook Pro since 2016.

The PROLED XDR display comes in 14.2-and 16.3-inch sizes, with ProMotion allowing for refresh rates between 10 Hz and 120 Hz. Apple claims 2,000 nits of peak brightness and a 10,000,000:1 contrast ratio for intensely deep blacks.

The 14-inch MacBook Pro is 3 pounds, about half a pound less than the existing version, while the 16-inch MacBook Pro is 4 pounds, or 0.7 pounds lighter than it was before. Apple's bezels are also less noticeable than before. The hinge seems to be a point of pride (that's the second time this month, after the iPhone Duo). In this case, it's that the screen is less prone to wobble when you touch it.

The new laptops are only slightly thinner than their predecessor. Apple claims that the 16-inch model is "nearly a millimeter thinner" and the 14-incher is "half a millimeter thinner." Apple attributes those shavings to OLED's display stack.

Apple's own apps are already set to work with touch out of the box, and the company says many other apps will already work right away, including Notion, Canva, Zoom, Microsoft Word, Excel, PowerPoint, Adobe Lightroom, DaVinci Resolve, Blender, and more.

Apple already had the best speakers in a laptop, and now it's promising improvements: 50% deeper bass and new tweeters for clearer sound. There's even dedicated audio tuning for people who want to use the speakers with their laptop lid closed.

The significant change to the Mac is another in a flurry of launches for new CEO John Ternus, who also recently introduced the iPhone 18 Pro; the foldable iPhone Duo; Apple Watch Series 12 and Ultra 4; HomeView; and a new iPad Mini, also with an OLED panel.

The devices follow a long resistance to touchscreen laptops from Apple. Former CEO Steve Jobs, at an event introducing Mac OS X Lion in 2010, called laptops with touchscreens "ergonomically terrible" , claiming that "after an extended period of time, your arm wants to fall off." (HomeView, Apple's smart home manager, has a vertical touchscreen and no one has made a peep about that. The iPad, too, has been vertical on Apple's keyboards, though some of those include touchpads as well).

The Mac resisted a touchscreen throughout former CEO Tim Cook's tenure, as well, though these new laptops definitely were developed under his leadership. In the last decade, touchscreens have become a common feature on laptops running Windows, and Microsoft's latest operating system, Windows 11 , was designed to be slightly more touch-friendly than its predecessors.

passages: After years of resisting, Apple today launched a MacBook Pro with a touchscreen starting at $2,899.
The new Touchscreen MacBook marks two marquee product launches for new CEO John Ternus, who also introduced the company’s first foldable, the iPhone Duo, in September .

extraction.body: After years of resisting, Apple today launched a MacBook Pro with a touchscreen starting at $2,899. The release comes nearly 10 years after the company first tried integrating touchscreens on its laptops, with its Touch Bar on a MacBook Pro , which it later went on to remove . The new MacBook Pro more fully embraces the touchscreen, offering a new PROLED XDR Display in both 14-inch and 16-inch screen sizes. The device is powered by M5 Pro and M5 Max chips as options to choose from, along with up to 128GB of unified memory and up to 16TB of storage. The display has 2,000 nits peak HDR and SDR brightness and a 10,000,000:1 contrast ratio. To make the new MacBook easy to use, Apple designed a hinge that stabilizes the screen when users touch it. This also helps to stabilize the camera when you are on a video call and trying to access content on the display. In addition, the screen will include a Dynamic Island-style cutout instead of the notch that’s present on most of the current MacBooks. Plus, the new MacBook features a six-speaker array with a new woofer design for better sound. The 14-inch Pro weighs 3.0 pounds (1.38 kg), and the 16-inch Pro weighs 4.0 pounds (1.82 kg) — lighter than its non-touch predecessors. Both feature three Thunderbolt 5 ports, an HDMI port, an SDXC card slot, MagSafe, and a headphone jack. Users can hook up three external displays on the M5 Pro variant and up to four displays on the M5 Max variant. The Touchscreen MacBook Pro 14-inch starts at $2,899, and the 16-inch version starts at $3,399. Consumers can place a preorder for the new touchscreen MacBook Pro from October 30, and the device will be available starting November 6. The new Touchscreen MacBook marks two marquee product launches for new CEO John Ternus, who also introduced the company’s first foldable, the iPhone Duo, in September . Various Apple executives, including Steve Jobs and Tim Cook, have scoffed at the idea of a touchscreen Mac in the past. Jobs famously called the idea “ergonomically terrible” at one point. However, rumors of the company working on such a variant started circulating nearly three years before today’s introduction . The launch follows yesterday’s unveiling of a new standard MacBook Pro with the M6 chip in 14-inch size starting from $1,999 . sources.title: MacBook Pro: Apple launches its first ever touchscreen Mac – and brings back iconic feature - The Independent
passages: Apple has launched an entirely new version of the MacBook Pro, its first-ever touchscreen Mac, after years of saying that it would never make one .
But Apple appeared to stress the benefits of its new OLED display more than the touchscreen feature, stressing its brightness, contrast and colours.
The announcement comes at the end of a busy week, which has also seen Apple introduce a new iPad Mini, as well as updated iMacs and lower-end MacBook Pro models.
That is compared with a starting price of $1,999 for the non-touchscreen version, though that also includes a less powerful chip.
New touch sensitive laptop brings back glowing Apple logo on the back, alongside lighter design
The display allows for more vivid colours, blacker blacks and better contrast, Apple said.
All of those new features and changes are enabled by a new screen technology that Apple calls PROLED XDR.
The introduction of touch will allow users to more easily do normal actions such as moving windows around, scrolling, and placing content, Apple said.

But it suggested it would also open up new ways of interacting with the Mac entirely, such as letting artists draw on it, musicians play software instruments with the screen, and allowing developers to test their apps as if they were being used on an iPhone or iPad.
Many other companies have long offered touchscreen laptops.

That is despite the fact that many of its executives, including new chief executive John Ternus, have previously dismissed the idea – primarily because of the ergonomic troubles of reaching out across the keyboard to touch the display.
It comes amid a broader push into new kinds of formats for its devices, including a new foldable phone and display for the home.

extraction.body: Apple has finally brought touchscreen support to the MacBook Pro, ending its long-standing resistance to adding touch controls to its laptops. Announced at the company's “Pro and tell” event on Wednesday, the new MacBook Pro features an OLED display, support for touch gestures and Apple's M5 Pro and M5 Max processors. The laptop also gets a redesigned interface and a lighter build.In India, the new MacBook Pro is priced at Rs 3,49,900 for the 14-inch model and Rs 4,09,900 for the 16-inch variant. The laptop is scheduled to be available from November 9.Apple MacBook Pro: What's new A look at Apple's first-ever touchscreen laptop.The touchscreen is the biggest change to Apple's professional laptop. Apple says the feature will also benefit professional workflows, allowing designers to interact with 3D models and music producers to adjust controls using their fingers.Apple has redesigned the interface to make touch interactions more natural while retaining the traditional keyboard and trackpad experience. The new MacBook Pro also introduces Dynamic Island, bringing a familiar iPhone feature to the Mac. It provides access to Spotlight search, Live Activities, music controls and other information from the top of the screen.The laptop uses a tandem OLED display, which Apple calls PROLED XDR. The display supports a refresh rate of up to 120Hz through ProMotion, with peak brightness reaching 2,000 nits for HDR content. Apple is also offering a nano-texture option to reduce reflections.The new models are powered by the M5 Pro and M5 Max chips, which are designed for demanding tasks such as video editing, 3D rendering, software development and AI workloads. Apple says the processors include Neural Accelerators in their GPU cores to speed up AI-related tasks. Storage configurations go up to 16TB, with the company claiming up to twice the storage speed.Other upgrades include a redesigned thermal system, an improved six-speaker audio setup, a studio-quality three-microphone array and support for Wi-Fi 7 and Bluetooth 6. The laptop retains ports such as HDMI, an SDXC card slot, MagSafe 3 and a headphone jack, alongside three Thunderbolt 5 ports.Apple claims the new MacBook Pro offers up to 24 hours of battery life and can charge to 50 per cent in 30 minutes. The redesigned models are also lighter than their predecessors.A major change in Apple's laptop strategyApple's decision is notable because the company has resisted touchscreen Macs for years. In 2010, Steve Jobs described touchscreen laptops as “ergonomically terrible”. Two years later, former CEO Tim Cook argued against combining tablets and laptops, comparing the idea to converging a toaster and a refrigerator.Apple later experimented with the Touch Bar, a touch-sensitive strip that replaced the function keys on MacBook Pro models introduced in 2016. However, the company brought back physical function keys in its 2021 redesign and discontinued the Touch Bar in 2023.The new MacBook Pro represents a significant change in that approach, bringing direct touch interaction to Apple's flagship laptop while keeping its established keyboard-and-trackpad controls.- Ends

coreStoryFacts.text: The 14-inch and 16-inch MacBook Pros are available for pre-order now and will ship on Nov.
The 14-incher will start at $2,899, while the 16-incher will start at $3,399.
The systems use Apple's existing M5 Pro and M5 Max chips, and go up to 16TB of storage and 128GB of memory.
These systems also feature the first redesigns for the MacBook Pro since 2021, when the M1 Pro and M1 Max launched in what has become a familiar design with a notch.
These new models include the Dynamic Island around the webcam, similar to the iPhone, which can be used for real-time notifications.

The new laptops are only slightly thinner than their predecessor.

Apple claims 2,000 nits of peak brightness and a 10,000,000:1 contrast ratio for intensely deep blacks.

Apple's own apps are already set to work with touch out of the box, and the company says many other apps will already work right away, including Notion, Canva, Zoom, Microsoft Word, Excel, PowerPoint, Adobe Lightroom, DaVinci Resolve, Blender, and more.
Apple already had the best speakers in a laptop, and now it's promising improvements: 50% deeper bass and new tweeters for clearer sound.
There's even dedicated audio tuning for people who want to use the speakers with their laptop lid closed.
After years of resisting, Apple today launched a MacBook Pro with a touchscreen starting at $2,899.
The new Touchscreen MacBook marks two marquee product launches for new CEO John Ternus, who also introduced the company’s first foldable, the iPhone Duo, in September .
Various Apple executives, including Steve Jobs and Tim Cook, have scoffed at the idea of a touchscreen Mac in the past.
The new MacBook Pro more fully embraces the touchscreen, offering a new PROLED XDR Display in both 14-inch and 16-inch screen sizes.
The device is powered by M5 Pro and M5 Max chips as options to choose from, along with up to 128GB of unified memory and up to 16TB of storage.
The display has 2,000 nits peak HDR and SDR brightness and a 10,000,000:1 contrast ratio.
This also helps to stabilize the camera when you are on a video call and trying to access content on the display.
Apple has launched an entirely new version of the MacBook Pro, its first-ever touchscreen Mac, after years of saying that it would never make one .
But Apple appeared to stress the benefits of its new OLED display more than the touchscreen feature, stressing its brightness, contrast and colours.
The announcement comes at the end of a busy week, which has also seen Apple introduce a new iPad Mini, as well as updated iMacs and lower-end MacBook Pro models.
That is compared with a starting price of $1,999 for the non-touchscreen version, though that also includes a less powerful chip.
New touch sensitive laptop brings back glowing Apple logo on the back, alongside lighter design
The display allows for more vivid colours, blacker blacks and better contrast, Apple said.
All of those new features and changes are enabled by a new screen technology that Apple calls PROLED XDR.
The introduction of touch will allow users to more easily do normal actions such as moving windows around, scrolling, and placing content, Apple said.

But it suggested it would also open up new ways of interacting with the Mac entirely, such as letting artists draw on it, musicians play software instruments with the screen, and allowing developers to test their apps as if they were being used on an iPhone or iPad.
Many other companies have long offered touchscreen laptops.

That is despite the fact that many of its executives, including new chief executive John Ternus, have previously dismissed the idea – primarily because of the ergonomic troubles of reaching out across the keyboard to touch the display.
It comes amid a broader push into new kinds of formats for its devices, including a new foldable phone and display for the home.

The laptop is scheduled to be available from November 9.Apple MacBook Pro: What's new A look at Apple's first-ever touchscreen laptop.The touchscreen is the biggest change to Apple's professional laptop.
Apple has finally brought touchscreen support to the MacBook Pro, ending its long-standing resistance to adding touch controls to its laptops.

Two years later, former CEO Tim Cook argued against combining tablets and laptops, comparing the idea to converging a toaster and a refrigerator.Apple later experimented with the Touch Bar, a touch-sensitive strip that replaced the function keys on MacBook Pro models introduced in 2016.

Apple says the feature will also benefit professional workflows, allowing designers to interact with 3D models and music producers to adjust controls using their fingers.Apple has redesigned the interface to make touch interactions more natural while retaining the traditional keyboard and trackpad experience.

Apple is also offering a nano-texture option to reduce reflections.The new models are powered by the M5 Pro and M5 Max chips, which are designed for demanding tasks such as video editing, 3D rendering, software development and AI workloads.
It provides access to Spotlight search, Live Activities, music controls and other information from the top of the screen.The laptop uses a tandem OLED display, which Apple calls PROLED XDR.

Apple claims 2,000 nits of peak brightness and a 10,000,000:1 contrast ratio for intensely deep blacks.

Apple's own apps are already set to work with touch out of the box, and the company says many other apps will already work right away, including Notion, Canva, Zoom, Microsoft Word, Excel, PowerPoint, Adobe Lightroom, DaVinci Resolve, Blender, and more.
Apple already had the best speakers in a laptop, and now it's promising improvements: 50% deeper bass and new tweeters for clearer sound.
There's even dedicated audio tuning for people who want to use the speakers with their laptop lid closed.
After years of resisting, Apple today launched a MacBook Pro with a touchscreen starting at $2,899.
The new Touchscreen MacBook marks two marquee product launches for new CEO John Ternus, who also introduced the company’s first foldable, the iPhone Duo, in September .
Various Apple executives, including Steve Jobs and Tim Cook, have scoffed at the idea of a touchscreen Mac in the past.
The new MacBook Pro more fully embraces the touchscreen, offering a new PROLED XDR Display in both 14-inch and 16-inch screen sizes.
The device is powered by M5 Pro and M5 Max chips as options to choose from, along with up to 128GB of unified memory and up to 16TB of storage.
The display has 2,000 nits peak HDR and SDR brightness and a 10,000,000:1 contrast ratio.
This also helps to stabilize the camera when you are on a video call and trying to access content on the display.
Apple has launched an entirely new version of the MacBook Pro, its first-ever touchscreen Mac, after years of saying that it would never make one .
But Apple appeared to stress the benefits of its new OLED display more than the touchscreen feature, stressing its brightness, contrast and colours.
The announcement comes at the end of a busy week, which has also seen Apple introduce a new iPad Mini, as well as updated iMacs and lower-end MacBook Pro models.
That is compared with a starting price of $1,999 for the non-touchscreen version, though that also includes a less powerful chip.
New touch sensitive laptop brings back glowing Apple logo on the back, alongside lighter design
The display allows for more vivid colours, blacker blacks and better contrast, Apple said.
All of those new features and changes are enabled by a new screen technology that Apple calls PROLED XDR.
The introduction of touch will allow users to more easily do normal actions such as moving windows around, scrolling, and placing content, Apple said.

But it suggested it would also open up new ways of interacting with the Mac entirely, such as letting artists draw on it, musicians play software instruments with the screen, and allowing developers to test their apps as if they were being used on an iPhone or iPad.
Many other companies have long offered touchscreen laptops.

That is despite the fact that many of its executives, including new chief executive John Ternus, have previously dismissed the idea – primarily because of the ergonomic troubles of reaching out across the keyboard to touch the display.
It comes amid a broader push into new kinds of formats for its devices, including a new foldable phone and display for the home.

The laptop is scheduled to be available from November 9.Apple MacBook Pro: What's new A look at Apple's first-ever touchscreen laptop.The touchscreen is the biggest change to Apple's professional laptop.
Apple has finally brought touchscreen support to the MacBook Pro, ending its long-standing resistance to adding touch controls to its laptops.

Two years later, former CEO Tim Cook argued against combining tablets and laptops, comparing the idea to converging a toaster and a refrigerator.Apple later experimented with the Touch Bar, a touch-sensitive strip that replaced the function keys on MacBook Pro models introduced in 2016.

Apple says the feature will also benefit professional workflows, allowing designers to interact with 3D models and music producers to adjust controls using their fingers.Apple has redesigned the interface to make touch interactions more natural while retaining the traditional keyboard and trackpad experience.

Apple is also offering a nano-texture option to reduce reflections.The new models are powered by the M5 Pro and M5 Max chips, which are designed for demanding tasks such as video editing, 3D rendering, software development and AI workloads.
It provides access to Spotlight search, Live Activities, music controls and other information from the top of the screen.The laptop uses a tandem OLED display, which Apple calls PROLED XDR.

coreFacts.text: The 14-inch and 16-inch MacBook Pros are available for pre-order now and will ship on Nov.
The 14-incher will start at $2,899, while the 16-incher will start at $3,399.
The systems use Apple's existing M5 Pro and M5 Max chips, and go up to 16TB of storage and 128GB of memory.
These systems also feature the first redesigns for the MacBook Pro since 2021, when the M1 Pro and M1 Max launched in what has become a familiar design with a notch.
These new models include the Dynamic Island around the webcam, similar to the iPhone, which can be used for real-time notifications.
At an event in Los Angeles, the company detailed its new MacBook Pros featuring OLED XDR displays that you can control with your fingers.
Apple's bezels are also less noticeable than before.
The hinge seems to be a point of pride (that's the second time this month, after the iPhone Duo).
In this case, it's that the screen is less prone to wobble when you touch it.
The new laptops are only slightly thinner than their predecessor.

Apple finally has touchscreen laptops. At an event in Los Angeles, the company detailed its new MacBook Pros featuring OLED XDR displays that you can control with your fingers. The 14-inch and 16-inch MacBook Pros are available for pre-order now and will ship on Nov. 6. The 14-incher will start at $2,899, while the 16-incher will start at $3,399. The systems use Apple's existing M5 Pro and M5 Max chips, and go up to 16TB of storage and 128GB of memory. These systems also feature the first redesigns for the MacBook Pro since 2021, when the M1 Pro and M1 Max launched in what has become a familiar design with a notch. These new models include the Dynamic Island around the webcam, similar to the iPhone, which can be used for real-time notifications. They also have light-up Apple logos, which we haven't seen on a MacBook Pro since 2016. The PROLED XDR display comes in 14.2-and 16.3-inch sizes, with ProMotion allowing for refresh rates between 10 Hz and 120 Hz. Apple claims 2,000 nits of peak brightness and a 10,000,000:1 contrast ratio for intensely deep blacks. The 14-inch MacBook Pro is 3 pounds, about half a pound less than the existing version, while the 16-inch MacBook Pro is 4 pounds, or 0.7 pounds lighter than it was before. Apple's bezels are also less noticeable than before. The hinge seems to be a point of pride (that's the second time this month, after the iPhone Duo). In this case, it's that the screen is less prone to wobble when you touch it. The new laptops are only slightly thinner than their predecessor. Apple claims that the 16-inch model is "nearly a millimeter thinner" and the 14-incher is "half a millimeter thinner." Apple attributes those shavings to OLED's display stack. Apple's own apps are already set to work with touch out of the box, and the company says many other apps will already work right away, including Notion, Canva, Zoom, Microsoft Word, Excel, PowerPoint, Adobe Lightroom, DaVinci Resolve, Blender, and more. Apple already had the best speakers in a laptop, and now it's promising improvements: 50% deeper bass and new tweeters for clearer sound. There's even dedicated audio tuning for people who want to use the speakers with their laptop lid closed. The significant change to the Mac is another in a flurry of launches for new CEO John Ternus, who also recently introduced the iPhone 18 Pro; the foldable iPhone Duo; Apple Watch Series 12 and Ultra 4; HomeView; and a new iPad Mini, also with an OLED panel. The devices follow a long resistance to touchscreen laptops from Apple. Former CEO Steve Jobs, at an event introducing Mac OS X Lion in 2010, called laptops with touchscreens "ergonomically terrible" , claiming that "after an extended period of time, your arm wants to fall off." (HomeView, Apple's smart home manager, has a vertical touchscreen and no one has made a peep about that. The iPad, too, has been vertical on Apple's keyboards, though some of those include touchpads as well). The Mac resisted a touchscreen throughout former CEO Tim Cook's tenure, as well, though these new laptops definitely were developed under his leadership. In the last decade, touchscreens have become a common feature on laptops running Windows, and Microsoft's latest operating system, Windows 11 , was designed to be slightly more touch-friendly than its predecessors. relevantPassages.text: The 14-inch and 16-inch MacBook Pros are available for pre-order now and will ship on Nov.
The 14-incher will start at $2,899, while the 16-incher will start at $3,399.
The systems use Apple's existing M5 Pro and M5 Max chips, and go up to 16TB of storage and 128GB of memory.
These systems also feature the first redesigns for the MacBook Pro since 2021, when the M1 Pro and M1 Max launched in what has become a familiar design with a notch.
These new models include the Dynamic Island around the webcam, similar to the iPhone, which can be used for real-time notifications.
At an event in Los Angeles, the company detailed its new MacBook Pros featuring OLED XDR displays that you can control with your fingers.
Apple's bezels are also less noticeable than before.
The hinge seems to be a point of pride (that's the second time this month, after the iPhone Duo).
In this case, it's that the screen is less prone to wobble when you touch it.
The new laptops are only slightly thinner than their predecessor.
